verdicts.reason: A is just the square shrunk into the tall canvas: the attribution and logo are tiny, the product is a small object in the bottom corner, and the middle third is dead space. B fills the format better and has larger text, but it puts the product above the quote, so the reading order is off. B's quote and attribution also sit on the decorative circle, the quote mark floats far above its text, and the text is jammed against the left edge (about 17px).

A keeps the reading order (logo, quote mark, quote, attribution, then product sitting on the circle, as in the original). However, the centred logo and product clash with the left-aligned text, and the left margin is very tight (about 17px). B puts the product before the quote and runs the quote and attribution over the circle. The quote mark is stranded with a large gap above the text, the left margin is cramped, and the logo is pushed off-centre to the right.

A has a sensible top-to-bottom order with comfortable 30px margins and the product resting on the circle as in the original. The logo floats right while the text is left-aligned, and there is some dead space above the quote. B leads with the product, sets the quote and attribution over the decorative circle, and leaves a large gap between the quote mark and the quote, so the hierarchy is inverted.

A has the product first, a quote mark stranded far above the quote, and the quote and attribution sitting over the background circle. B keeps the original order (quote, attribution, then product on the circle) with no collisions. B's flaws are a centred logo and product against left-aligned text and a tight left margin of about 17px.
